key_insight: Porting the AHBR range-separated hybrid vdW-DF functional from Quantum Espresso to VASP enables stable stress-based unit-cell optimization for accurate structure prediction across molecules, solids, and soft matter.
engineering_relevance: This makes high-accuracy DFT more practical for materials discovery workflows that need reliable geometry relaxation, cohesion, and stacking predictions in complex matter.
method: Implemented the AHBR XC functional in VASP, where stress-based optimization is already robust for RSHs.
Benchmarked AHBR-VASP against AHBR-QE on non-covalent molecular interactions and simple bulk structure/cohesion.
Applied the new implementation to distorted-rocksalt metal monoxides and C2N COF stacking motifs.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports cross-code validation against high-accuracy AHBR-QE results and demonstrations on benchmark systems plus two application classes: distorted-rocksalt monoxides and C2N COF layer stacking.
watch_item: The main caution is that the original QE implementation was not robust for stress-based optimization of RSHs, so implementation details and code-specific behavior remain important.
paper_title: Stress-based structure optimization for a range-separated hybrid van der Waals density functional
